result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`"java"`, `"js"`), and the landscape merges old `"  *.java"` data with new `"java"` data. The codeanalyzer and reports test suites pass offline (332 codeanalyzer tests, 0 failures).

What changed:

- **Producer** (`SourceCodeAspectUtils.getAspectsPerExtensions`): the per-extension aspect is named `extension` instead of `"  *." + extension`. This also changes the names of the per-extension scopes from `getScopesWithExtensions`, which the code browser lists.
- **Metrics and summary** (`AnalysisUtils`): the `.replace("*.", "")` on the metric name is gone. The metric ids stay the same because `getMetricId` already turns the old two-space prefix into nothing, so `LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` comes out identical. I checked this by reading `getMetricId`, not by diffing a full analysis run. The indented `  *.java: N files, …` summary line is kept as it was.
- **Landscape** (`LandscapeAnalysisResults`): a new `getExtensionName` helper strips `*.`, trims and lower-cases. It is used in the per-repository loop, which covers the main path, and in `merge`, which covers the build/generated/other merge. Each repository still contributes one description entry to a merged entry.
- **Tests**: `CodeConfigurationTest` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` now assert the bare names. I also added `LandscapeAnalysisResultsTest` with two cases: old and new spellings merging on the main path, and build plus other merging with a two-repository breakdown.

I left the existing `.replace("*.", "")` calls in the report code (`SummaryUtils`, `OverviewReportGenerator`, `LandscapeReportGenerator` and others). They are now no-ops on fresh data, so removing them would be a separate cleanup. Nothing is committed.
